metadata.blurb: Exodus is a self-custody desktop, mobile, and browser crypto wallet with multi-chain asset support.

ref.explanation: Exodus says users fully control their wallet, 12-word secret key, and private keys.
Exodus support pages reviewed for this entry did not show ENS-name recipient resolution.
Targeted review of Exodus support pages found address and QR-code transfer flows, but no ENS recipient-resolution support.
Exodus supports swaps for thousands of crypto pairs directly in the wallet.
Exodus describes support for 50+ crypto networks with assets managed from one wallet.
Exodus Web3 Wallet connects to dapps and requires signing wallet requests.
Exodus publishes some open-source packages but not the full consumer wallet app source as a single open-source wallet repository.
Exodus supports separate Exodus and hardware-wallet portfolios, plus wallet restoration from the same 12-word secret key.
Exodus documents product usage and performance data collection, while the App Store privacy label lists Usage Data.
Exodus documents product usage and performance data collection.
Exodus says its coordinated vulnerability disclosure program is operated via its HackerOne bug bounty program.
Exodus says users can set a password to protect the secret key on the device.
Exodus supports Trezor on desktop and Ledger on mobile.
Exodus explains that balance and transaction information is displayed by querying blockchain data providers, not through an embedded Ethereum L1 light client.
Exodus security and Web3 Wallet docs reviewed for this entry did not show malicious-contract registry warnings before signing.
Exodus Web3 Wallet docs warn users to check official websites, but no wallet-level known-scam URL warning feature was found.
Exodus support docs reviewed for this entry did not show risky-recipient warnings before sending.
Exodus Web3 Wallet docs say users approve transaction requests, but no simulation preview feature was found.
Exodus says it is not yet possible to remove previously approved infinite approvals or adjust the amount a transaction is approving.
Exodus public docs reviewed for this entry did not show user-selected self-hosted-node transaction broadcast.
Exodus publishes release hashes for downloadable app releases.
Exodus publishes a public version history and release notes page.
Exodus publishes release hashes, but no reproducible-build instructions or attestations for the full consumer wallet apps were found.
Exodus official site says Exodus is available on desktop Windows/macOS/Linux, mobile iOS/Android, and as a browser extension.
Exodus says it is available on desktop for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Exodus says it is available on mobile for iOS and Android.
Exodus says it is available as a browser extension.
Exodus is an app/browser-extension wallet, not a browser-native wallet.
Exodus ships as desktop, mobile, and a browser extension (Exodus Web3 Wallet); there is no browser-based web app usable without installing an app or extension.
Exodus says mobile availability includes iOS.
Exodus says mobile availability includes Android.
Exodus getting-started and assets docs state 50+ crypto networks and mention Ethereum, Solana, Bitcoin, and other supported networks.
Exodus Web3 Wallet connects to Ethereum and other supported Web3 networks.
Exodus Web3 Wallet connects to Solana and other supported networks.
Exodus homepage lists Bitcoin among supported assets.
Exodus has a dedicated Cosmos ATOM wallet supporting send/receive/stake of native ATOM.
Exodus lists SUI as a supported native asset (Sui and TON went live for send/receive/swap).
Exodus natively supports Aptos (APT) including APT staking via its knowledge base and asset list.
Exodus offers a dedicated XRP wallet supporting native XRP on the XRP Ledger.
Exodus has a dedicated ADA Cardano wallet supporting native manage/send/stake of ADA since 2020.
Exodus says it supports 50+ crypto networks with unlimited token support on popular Web3 networks.
Exodus getting-started guide says Web3 Wallet connects to dApps on Ethereum, Solana, and supported networks; mobile web3 browser/WalletConnect is limited to wallets created before April 22, 2026.
Exodus Mobile has web3 browser/WalletConnect for wallets created before April 22, 2026.
Exodus Web3 Wallet supports direct dApp connections; mobile has web3 browser or WalletConnect for grandfathered wallets.
Exodus buy guide says buy is available in Mobile, Desktop, and Web3 Wallet using credit/debit cards, bank account, PayPal, Apple Pay, and Google Pay through third-party API providers.
Exodus supports buying crypto directly in Mobile, Desktop, and Web3 Wallet.
Exodus getting-started guide says users can sell crypto directly using MoonPay.
Exodus buy guide lists bank account/bank transfers as payment methods.
Exodus buy guide lists credit and debit cards as payment methods.

Exodus buy guide lists Google Pay.

The consumer Exodus wallet onboards via a 12-word seed phrase; the passkey/MPC 'Passkeys Wallet' is a separate developer/embedded SDK product, not the consumer app's signup flow.
Exodus requires no personal information at signup and creates the wallet from a recovery phrase rather than an email address.
The consumer app requires creating or restoring a seed-phrase wallet before use, with no try/view-only guest mode.
The shipping consumer Exodus wallet is a seed-phrase self-custody wallet; the no-seed MPC 'Passkeys Wallet' is a separate embedded-wallet SDK for developers, not the consumer onboarding UX.
Exodus homepage and getting-started guide describe portfolio management, prices, performance tracking, NFTs, hardware portfolios, and multi-network assets.
Exodus describes monitoring portfolio assets across networks.
Exodus says users can track performance from anywhere.

Exodus's portfolio shows real-time balances, value and 24h/percentage performance but there is no evidence of acquisition cost-basis tracking, and reviews/support describe only current value and price-change tracking.
Exodus supports receiving and displaying NFTs in NFT Gallery on supported networks.
Exodus has an NFT Gallery for supported networks.
Exodus is a private-key self-custody wallet that only tracks addresses derived from your own seed, with no documented ability to add watch-only/view-only addresses you don't control.

Exodus lets users connect to DeFi lending protocols (e.g. Compound/Aave) via its Web3 dApp browser but there is no evidence it surfaces/reads existing external lending positions in its own portfolio UI.
Exodus surfaces staking or earn positions in wallet/portfolio views.
Exodus can connect to DEXs/LP dApps through its Web3 wallet but no source indicates it aggregates or displays external liquidity-pool positions within the wallet's portfolio view.
No evidence that Exodus surfaces or reads yield-vault positions (Yearn/Morpho-style) held in external protocols; its DeFi involvement is limited to dApp connectivity, not position tracking.
Exodus surfaces claimable rewards or earn balances.
Since Exodus does not surface external borrow/lending positions, there is no documented liquidation-risk warning feature for DeFi borrow positions.
Exodus staking guide says Exodus has built-in staking support for certain assets across Mobile, Desktop, and Web3 Wallet, with network-specific rules and lockups.
Exodus has built-in staking support for certain assets.
Exodus supports liquid staking of ETH via Lido (receiving stETH) through its Web3 wallet/mobile, as documented in its knowledge base.
Exodus staking automatically delegates to its third-party provider Everstake with no manual validator selection supported, per multiple staking guides.
Exodus displays estimated staking APY for stakeable assets in the wallet's staking section, as described in its support articles on staking and APY.
Exodus supports staking management directly from the wallet.
